transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2027-02-17 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Liu (Redwood CSM); Samir Kapoor (VP Eng), Leah Morgan (Head of ML), Daniel Ortiz (Infra), Rita Gomez (PM)

Summary:
Quick welcome + sprint-zero planning for integrating Redwood inference. Primary goals: validate network path for private deployment, agree staging benchmarks, define success criteria and timeline for pilot to production.

Topics:
1) Current infra and constraints (Kubernetes / EKS, on-prem data stores)
2) Security/compliance needs (SAML SSO, SOC2, KMS)
3) Pilot scope, benchmarks, and sampling prompts
4) Timeline and owners for sprint-zero tasks

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: All right, hey everyone thanks for joining, we have a small agenda, I'm Alex from Redwood, we'll do intros quick and then jump into sprint zero scope.
[00:12] Samir Kapoor: Thanks Alex, yeah Samir here, VP Eng at Silverleaf. We're trying to move from a prototype to a pilot for product search and personalization use cases.
[00:22] Rita Gomez: Hi all, Rita product, excited to see the runbook and what staging looks like.
[00:27] Alex Chen: Great. Priya, want to do a quick SE intro and what we'll cover technically?
[00:31] Priya Patel: Yeah hi everyone, Priya Patel, SE. We'll cover network routes for private deployments, recommended Dedicated vs Hosted for your throughput, baseline latency/cost expectations, and a small benchmark plan. Also we'll need the prompt set and some sample traffic pattern info.
[00:45] Leah Morgan: Quick note – our main constraint is PII redaction, plus we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. We're SOC2 pending so auditability is important.
[00:56] Jordan Liu: Noted. We have a standard audit log integration for Private mode, and we can route logs to your Kinesis or S3 bucket if that helps.
[01:06] Daniel Ortiz: On infra – we're on AWS EKS 1.24, private subnets, NAT egress for some services. We prefer VPC peering rather than public egress for the pilot. Is that supported for Redwood private?
[01:20] Priya Patel: Yes, VPC peering or PrivateLink are supported. For Private deployments we can do a customer-managed VPC with peering, and we support KMS integration for key management. There can be some ops work on routing but it's standard.
[01:34] Samir Kapoor: Okay good. Cost is a top question too — for search personalization we'll be calling fairly frequently, we need to understand cost profile for dedicated GPUs vs hosted pay-as-you-go.
[01:46] Alex Chen: Right. For throughput-heavy patterns we usually recommend Redwood Dedicated to keep unit costs predictable; the runbook will include capacity sizing examples. For initial pilot we often start with a small dedicated pool and can autoscale bursts.
[01:59] Rita Gomez: Can you share a sample sizing exercise? Like for 200 qps at 128 token avg what do we expect?
[02:08] Priya Patel: We'll run a quick calc in the bench plan, rough ballpark — depends on model choice and quantization. E.g., using an optimized 8-bit variant we might fit 80 to 120 qps per GPU for short seq lengths. We'll document assumptions.
[02:25] Leah Morgan: Also we have a preference for open models right now, want to keep vendor lock low. Do you have a model recommendation?
[02:33] Priya Patel: We can match an open family that's Redwood-verified for your latency targets — we include model variants and quant profiles in the runbook. We'll propose two variants: a lower-latency smaller model and a higher-quality model for A/B.
[02:48] Samir Kapoor: Sounds good. On timeline — Rita and I would like pilot up in staging within two weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[02:57] Alex Chen: Two weeks is aggressive but doable for sprint-zero if network and creds are ready. Typical sprint-zero is 2–3 weeks to validate networking, deploy a private agent, run a small benchmark, and finalize config.
[03:12] Daniel Ortiz: What's required from our side for networking? I can list out firewall rules and subnets.
[03:17] Priya Patel: We'll need CIDR ranges for peering, NAT/Egress policy doc if any blocked ports, and a service account or IAM role for the agent to pull model artifacts. We'll outline exact ports in the runbook.
[03:31] Rita Gomez: On the security front: SSO is via Okta, we use SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Can Redwood integrate with SCIM?
[03:41] Priya Patel: Yes, SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO are standard. For Private customers we also support customer-managed IdP and RBAC mapping.
[03:49] Leah Morgan: Encryption at rest – do you support bringing our own keys with KMS/HSM?
[03:54] Priya Patel: Yes, we integrate with external KMS; you can bring keys. For on-prem we can also support HSM integrations.
[04:03] Samir Kapoor: Great. Let's talk about benchmarks — what does Redwood need from us?
[04:08] Priya Patel: Representative prompts (a sample set of about 200–500 prompts), sample concurrent users pattern, and a staging dataset for evaluation. We'll run latency and token-cost benchmarks and produce a small report.
[04:20] Leah Morgan: For evaluation, our main success metrics are 95th percentile latency under 300ms for short responses, and model accuracy on our relevance eval (we'll share). Cost target is aspirational right now.
[04:33] Alex Chen: We'll capture those SLOs in the pilot plan. Also want to call out graceful degradation: if Dedicated capacity gets saturated we can fallback to hosted versions but we'll need to align on fallback policies.
[04:47] Daniel Ortiz: Are fallbacks automatic? How are secrets / keys protected during fallback?
[04:53] Priya Patel: Fallbacks are policy-driven; during fallback network path is the same if you use Private with hybrid fallback, but some customers choose to disable fallback for strict data residency. We'll include options and security tradeoffs.
[05:07] Alex Chen: Quick check — Leah, you mentioned audit logs to SIEM earlier. Do you have a preferred format?
[05:13] Leah Morgan: JSON lines to S3 is fine, or streamed to our Kinesis. We want 90-day retention minimum, with the ability to query traces.
[05:22] Jordan Liu: We can set retention settings and forwarding; Redwood Console supports trace links and token-level cost breakdown.
[05:29] Rita Gomez: What about model version pinning and rollouts? We need a safe way to roll out changes to models and revert.
[05:36] Priya Patel: Redwood supports version pinning and can do canary rollouts per route. We'll show the console workflow in the demo.
[05:44] Samir Kapoor: Excellent. Okay let's carve out a concrete sprint-zero checklist — what are the must-haves to start?
[05:51] Alex Chen: Must-haves: network diagram + CIDRs, Okta SAML + SCIM admin contact, sample prompt set and traffic patterns, staging EKS cluster access or deployable agent, and a signed pilot SOW for dedicated capacity if you choose that route.
[06:06] Daniel Ortiz: On the cluster access, we prefer to run a Redwood agent in our VPC rather than you having direct access. Is agent-based onboarding supported?
[06:14] Priya Patel: Yes that's common. The agent pulls model artifacts, communicates over the peered link, and keys remain in your KMS. We'll provide the agent container and Helm chart.
[06:25] Rita Gomez: Can we see a sample Helm chart and values?
[06:28] Priya Patel: We'll attach that to the runbook.
[06:31] Samir Kapoor: Who owns the SOW for pilot — is that sales or CS?
[06:35] Alex Chen: I'll own the commercial SOW and pricing, Jordan will coordinate onboarding deliverables. We'll get a pilot SOW template over after this call.
[06:44] Leah Morgan: On A/B testing — we want to test two model variants behind feature flags so product can route a percentage. Do you support route-level weighting?
[06:53] Priya Patel: Yes route-level weighting and rollout policies are supported in Redwood Console. We'll demo the UI for traffic split.
[07:01] Alex Chen: Quick break in flow: I'm going to outline timeline assumptions in the runbook, but Rita's ask for two weeks to staging — to hit that, customer needs network diagram and Okta contact by Friday.
[07:13] Rita Gomez: We can try for that, Rit a will coordinate the Okta admin.
[07:18] Samir Kapoor: Also, we may ask Redwood to run a small functional smoke test in staging. Do you have an automation script for that?
[07:25] Priya Patel: Yes, we provide a smoke test harness that hits a few endpoints and checks latencies and correctness. We'll give you a runbook to run the harness locally or we can run it from our side if permitted.
[07:38] Daniel Ortiz: Any privacy concerns with sending prompt data to Redwood for benchmarking? We need PII redaction and potentially runable on-prem.
[07:46] Priya Patel: We can redact PII before upload, or run the benchmarks in your VPC in Private mode so data never leaves your network. We'll include both options.
[07:57] Alex Chen: Okay, let's capture explicit owners (we'll also add these to the action items): Alex to send runbook and SOW template; Priya to create bench script; Daniel to provide networking; Leah to provide prompts and eval criteria; Rita to provide Okta contact.
[08:14] Rita Gomez: Sounds good. A few quick clarifications: how long does it take to spin up a dedicated pool once SOW signed?
[08:22] Alex Chen: Typically 3–7 business days for initial capacity allocation depending on GPU type and region. We'll call that out in SOW.
[08:30] Samir Kapoor: If we find the throughput higher than expected can we scale mid-pilot?
[08:34] Priya Patel: Yes autoscale and burst options exist, but cost and latency tradeoffs vary; we'll run a few scenarios in the sizing doc.
[08:45] Leah Morgan: One more question — debugging traces: can we correlate requests from our app to Redwood traces?
[08:51] Jordan Liu: We support trace hooks and correlation IDs — we can pass an X-Request-ID through the API and Console will show token-level traces.
[08:59] Daniel Ortiz: Great. On the legal/compliance path — do you have a standard DPA and security packet? We'll need SOC2 docs and pen test summary.
[09:08] Alex Chen: Yes we'll attach the security packet and DPA; our legal team can fast-track an NDA if needed.
[09:16] Samir Kapoor: Perfect. Any blockers we foresee?
[09:19] Priya Patel: The main blocker would be delayed network artifacts or Okta admin access; otherwise it's procedural.
[09:26] Rita Gomez: Okay let's wrap with a short recap and deliverables.
[09:30] Alex Chen: Recap — Redwood to send runbook, SOW template, Helm chart, benchmark harness. Silverleaf to share network diagram, Okta admin contact, prompt set, and success criteria. Owners and due dates we'll put in Jira after the call.
[09:44] Leah Morgan: One quick procedural ask: can you add a Slack channel for real-time updates?
[09:48] Jordan Liu: Yes we'll create a joint channel and invite the Silverleaf team.
[09:52] Samir Kapoor: That works. Thanks everyone, looking forward to the runbook.
[09:56] Alex Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the documents and schedule the baseline benchmark for the week of Feb 28.
